words.gloss: the wealth of the ear (gained by listening)

literal: Among wealth, the wealth is the wealth of the ear; that wealth, among all wealth, is supreme.
translation: The wealth of the ear, gained by listening to the wise, is the greatest of all wealth; that wealth is supreme among every other kind of treasure.
modern: செல்வங்களுள் சிறந்த செல்வம் காதால் கேட்டுப் பெறும் செல்வமே ஆகும்; அந்தச் செல்வம் மற்ற எல்லாச் செல்வங்களுள்ளும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet introduces the chapter on listening (hearing) by elevating it above all material possessions. The compound 'செவிச்செல்வம்' (wealth of the ear) refers to the wisdom and knowledge acquired by listening to learned people. The poet repeats the word 'செல்வம்' (wealth) multiple times to emphasize that listening is not merely a sensory act but the most valuable asset a person can acquire. Among all forms of worldly riches, this intellectual wealth is declared to be 'தலை' (supreme or foremost) because it cannot be stolen and guides one's life safely.
